text.p: Severe flooding continues in the US Northern Plains and upper Midwest from the eastern Dakotas into western Minnesota, also in southern Manitoba, Canada. Many rivers, especially the Red River near Fargo and Grand Forks, North Dakota, have continued to rise over the past few days and are at all-time record levels. Although no major storminess is expected during the next several days, this flooding situation is going to be very slow to diminish.
Tropical Storm Isa, with 70 mph winds, is in the western Pacific near 28n/147e, moving east at 18 mph. It is expected to weaken, become extratropical within 36 hours, and only threaten shipping.

Tropical Storm Jimmy, with 45 mph winds, is in the western Pacific near 15n/155e, moving northwest at 14 mph. It is expected to turn northward and intensify with top winds reaching 60 mph during the next 36 hours, but it will only be a threat to shipping.
There are no further statements at this time.
